front: A apuração levou oito meses e envolveu centenas de documentos.
pronunciation: ah ah-poo-rah-SOWNG leh-VOH OY-too MEH-zeez ee ehn-vohl-VEH-oo sehn-TEH-nahz jee doh-koo-MEHN-toos.
back: The investigation took eight months and involved hundreds of documents.
context: 'Apuração' = the reporting/fact-gathering behind a story. 'Apurar' = to look into, verify.

front: O jornal deu o furo antes de todos os concorrentes.
pronunciation: oo zhohr-NOW DEH-oo oo FOO-roo AHN-cheez jee TOH-dooz ooz kohn-koh-RREHN-chees.
back: The newspaper broke the story before all its competitors.
context: 'Furo (de reportagem)' = scoop. 'Dar o furo' = to break the story first.

front: A fonte pediu para não ser identificada.
pronunciation: ah FOHN-chee peh-JEE-oo PAH-rah NOWNG SEHR ee-dehn-chee-fee-KAH-dah.
back: The source asked not to be identified.
context: Protecting sources ('sigilo da fonte') is guaranteed by the Brazilian Constitution.

front: Ele falou em off, então a declaração não pode ser atribuída a ele.
pronunciation: EH-lee fah-LOH eng OHF, ehn-TOWNG ah deh-klah-rah-SOWNG NOWNG POH-jee SEHR ah-tree-boo-EE-dah ah EH-lee.
back: He spoke off the record, so the statement can't be attributed to him.
context: 'Falar em off' = to speak off the record (from English). 'On' = on the record.

front: Procurada pela reportagem, a empresa não se manifestou até o fechamento desta edição.
pronunciation: proh-koo-RAH-dah PEH-lah rreh-pohr-TAH-zheng, ah ehm-PREH-zah NOWNG see mah-nee-fehs-TOH ah-TEH oo feh-shah-MEHN-too DEHS-tah eh-jee-SOWNG.
back: When contacted by our reporters, the company had not commented by the time this edition went to press.
context: A formula seen in almost every Brazilian news story. 'Manifestar-se' = to comment publicly.

front: O lide deve responder ao quê, quem, quando, onde, como e por quê.
pronunciation: oo LAHY-jee DEH-vee rrehs-pohn-DEHR ah-oo KEH, KENG, KWAHN-doo, OHN-jee, KOH-moo ee pohr KEH.
back: The lede must answer what, who, when, where, how and why.
context: 'Lide' (from 'lead') = the opening paragraph of a news story. Note 'por quê' with an accent at the end.

front: A reportagem investigativa revelou um esquema de desvio de verbas públicas.
pronunciation: ah rreh-pohr-TAH-zheng een-vehs-chee-gah-CHEE-vah rreh-veh-LOH oong ehs-KEH-mah jee jeez-VEE-oo jee VEHR-bahs POO-blee-kahs.
back: The investigative report uncovered a scheme to embezzle public funds.
context: 'Esquema' = scheme (often corrupt). 'Desvio de verbas' = embezzlement of funds.

front: Os jornalistas tiveram acesso aos dados pela Lei de Acesso à Informação.
pronunciation: ooz zhohr-nah-LEES-tahs chee-VEH-rowng ah-SEH-soo ah-ooz DAH-doos PEH-lah LAY jee ah-SEH-soo AH een-fohr-mah-SOWNG.
back: The journalists obtained the data through the Access to Information Law.
context: Brazil's LAI (2011) is the local equivalent of a Freedom of Information Act.

front: A matéria foi corrigida após a publicação, e o erro foi informado em nota.
pronunciation: ah mah-TEH-ryah FOY koh-rree-ZHEE-dah ah-POHZ ah poo-blee-kah-SOWNG, ee oo EH-rroo FOY een-fohr-MAH-doo eng NOH-tah.
back: The article was corrected after publication, and the error was acknowledged in a note.
context: 'Errata' or 'nota de correção'. Transparency about errors builds credibility.

front: O editorial expressa a opinião do jornal, não a dos repórteres.
pronunciation: oo eh-jee-toh-ree-OW ehs-PREH-sah ah oh-pee-nee-OWNG doo zhohr-NOW, NOWNG ah dooz rreh-POHR-teh-rees.
back: The editorial expresses the newspaper's opinion, not the reporters'.
context: 'A dos repórteres' = 'a opinião dos repórteres' (the noun is omitted after the article).

front: A coluna de opinião tem tom provocativo e assumidamente parcial.
pronunciation: ah koh-LOO-nah jee oh-pee-nee-OWNG teng TOHNG proh-voh-kah-CHEE-voo ee ah-soo-mee-dah-MEHN-chee pahr-see-OW.
back: The opinion column has a provocative and openly partisan tone.
context: 'Assumidamente' = openly, avowedly. 'Parcial' = biased, partisan (not 'partial').

front: A liberdade de imprensa é um pilar da democracia.
pronunciation: ah lee-behr-DAH-jee jee eem-PREHN-sah EH oong pee-LAHR dah deh-moh-krah-SEE-ah.
back: Freedom of the press is a pillar of democracy.
context: 'Imprensa' = the press. Brazil ranks poorly in journalist safety; many local reporters face threats.

front: O jornalista foi processado por difamação, mas acabou absolvido.
pronunciation: oo zhohr-nah-LEES-tah FOY proh-seh-SAH-doo pohr jee-fah-mah-SOWNG, mahz ah-kah-BOH ahb-sohl-VEE-doo.
back: The journalist was sued for defamation, but was eventually acquitted.
context: 'Ser processado' = to be sued/prosecuted. 'Absolvido' = acquitted.

front: A crônica brasileira mistura humor, lirismo e observação do cotidiano.
pronunciation: ah KROH-nee-kah brah-zee-LAY-rah mees-TOO-rah oo-MOHR, lee-REEZ-moo ee ohb-sehr-vah-SOWNG doo koh-chee-jee-AH-noo.
back: The Brazilian crônica mixes humor, lyricism and observation of everyday life.
context: The 'crônica' is a uniquely Brazilian newspaper genre, mastered by Rubem Braga, Fernando Sabino and Luis Fernando Verissimo.

front: A sátira usa o exagero para expor o absurdo da realidade.
pronunciation: ah SAH-chee-rah OO-zah oo eh-zah-ZHEH-roo PAH-rah ehs-POHR oo ahb-SOOR-doo dah rreh-ah-lee-DAH-jee.
back: Satire uses exaggeration to expose the absurdity of reality.
context: 'Expor' = to expose. Satire works when the audience recognizes the truth behind the exaggeration.

front: A manchete satírica era tão verossímil que muita gente acreditou.
pronunciation: ah mahn-SHEH-chee sah-CHEE-ree-kah EH-rah TOWNG veh-roh-SEE-mee-oo keh MOOY-tah ZHEHN-chee ah-kreh-jee-TOH.
back: The satirical headline was so plausible that many people believed it.
context: 'Verossímil' = plausible, believable. Satire sites like Sensacionalista are often mistaken for real news.

front: Ah, que maravilha: mais um aumento de imposto!
pronunciation: AH, keh mah-rah-VEE-lyah: MAHYZ oong ow-MEHN-too jee eem-POHS-too!
back: Oh, how wonderful: another tax increase!
context: Classic Brazilian sarcasm: praise for something obviously bad. Tone of voice does the work.

front: Parabéns aos envolvidos.
pronunciation: pah-rah-BENGZ ah-ooz ehn-vohl-VEE-doos.
back: Congratulations to everyone involved.
context: Ironic internet catchphrase used to mock an obviously bad result, like a disastrous project or a terrible decision.

front: Adorei esperar duas horas na fila. Só que não.
pronunciation: ah-doh-RAY ehs-peh-RAHR DOO-ahz OH-rahz nah FEE-lah. SOH keh NOWNG.
back: I loved waiting two hours in line. Not.
context: 'Só que não' (but no) flips the previous sentence into sarcasm. Very common in speech and on social media.

front: Tá bom, vou fingir que acredito.
pronunciation: TAH BOHNG, VOH feen-ZHEER keh ah-kreh-JEE-too.
back: Sure, I'll pretend I believe you.
context: Ironic reply to an obvious lie or excuse. 'Tá bom' (okay) can sound very sarcastic.

front: Imagina! Não foi trabalho nenhum.
pronunciation: ee-mah-ZHEE-nah! NOWNG FOY trah-BAH-lyoo neh-NYOONG.
back: Don't mention it! It was no trouble at all.
context: 'Imagina!' answers a thank-you, but tone matters: it can sincerely mean 'no problem' or ironically hint it was a lot of trouble.

front: Ironia do destino: o fiscal de trânsito foi multado por excesso de velocidade.
pronunciation: ee-roh-NEE-ah doo dehs-CHEE-noo: oo fees-KOW jee TRAHN-zee-too FOY mool-TAH-doo pohr eh-SEH-soo jee veh-loh-see-DAH-jee.
back: Irony of fate: the traffic warden was fined for speeding.
context: 'Ironia do destino' = situational irony. 'Ser multado' = to be fined.

front: O Brasil é o país do futuro, e sempre será.
pronunciation: oo brah-ZEE-oo EH oo pah-EES doo foo-TOO-roo, ee SEHM-pree seh-RAH.
back: Brazil is the country of the future, and always will be.
context: Self-deprecating joke on Stefan Zweig's 1941 book 'Brazil, a Land of the Future': the future that never arrives.

front: O texto é uma ironia fina, quase imperceptível para quem não conhece o contexto.
pronunciation: oo TEHS-too EH OO-mah ee-roh-NEE-ah FEE-nah, KWAH-zee eem-pehr-sehp-CHEE-vehl PAH-rah KENG NOWNG koh-NYEH-see oo kohn-TEHS-too.
back: The text is a subtle irony, almost imperceptible to anyone who doesn't know the context.
context: 'Ironia fina' = subtle, refined irony. Understanding it is a real C1 skill.

front: Nas entrelinhas, o colunista critica duramente o governo.
pronunciation: nahz ehn-treh-LEE-nyahs, oo koh-loo-NEES-tah kree-CHEE-kah doo-rah-MEHN-chee oo goh-VEHR-noo.
back: Between the lines, the columnist harshly criticizes the government.
context: 'Ler nas entrelinhas' = to read between the lines. A key skill during censorship.

front: O chargista resumiu a crise política em um único desenho.
pronunciation: oo shahr-ZHEES-tah rreh-zoo-MEE-oo ah KREE-zee poh-LEE-chee-kah eng oong OO-nee-koo deh-ZEH-nyoo.
back: The cartoonist summed up the political crisis in a single drawing.
context: 'Charge' = political cartoon; 'chargista' = cartoonist. 'Tirinha' = comic strip.

front: O Febeapá de Stanislaw Ponte Preta registrava as besteiras ditas por autoridades.
pronunciation: oo feh-beh-ah-PAH jee ehs-tah-nees-LAHF POHN-chee PREH-tah rreh-zhees-TRAH-vah ahz behs-TAY-rahz JEE-tahs pohr ow-toh-ree-DAH-jees.
back: Stanislaw Ponte Preta's Febeapá recorded the nonsense uttered by officials.
context: The 'Festival de Besteira que Assola o País' (1960s) is a classic of Brazilian satire. 'Besteira' = nonsense.

front: O humorista foi censurado por uma piada sobre o presidente.
pronunciation: oo oo-moh-REES-tah FOY sehn-soo-RAH-doo pohr OO-mah pee-AH-dah SOH-bree oo preh-zee-DEHN-chee.
back: The comedian was censored for a joke about the president.
context: Debates about the limits of humor ('limites do humor') are frequent in Brazil.

front: Uma coisa é fazer humor com o poder; outra é humilhar quem é vulnerável.
pronunciation: OO-mah KOY-zah EH fah-ZEHR oo-MOHR kohng oo poh-DEHR; OH-trah EH oo-mee-LYAHR KENG EH vool-neh-RAH-vehl.
back: Making fun of the powerful is one thing; humiliating the vulnerable is another.
context: 'Uma coisa é…; outra é…' = it's one thing to… and another to… The 'punching up vs punching down' debate.

front: A notícia viralizou, mas ninguém leu além da manchete.
pronunciation: ah noh-CHEE-syah vee-rah-lee-ZOH, mahs neen-GENG LEH-oo ah-LENG dah mahn-SHEH-chee.
back: The news went viral, but nobody read beyond the headline.
context: 'Viralizar' = to go viral. 'Além de' = beyond.

front: O clickbait promete muito e entrega pouco.
pronunciation: oo kleek-BAY-chee proh-MEH-chee MOOY-too ee ehn-TREH-gah POH-koo.
back: Clickbait promises a lot and delivers little.
context: Brazilians use 'clickbait' or 'caça-cliques'. 'Entregar' = to deliver.

front: A reportagem deu voz a quem raramente é ouvido.
pronunciation: ah rreh-pohr-TAH-zheng DEH-oo VOHS ah KENG rrah-rah-MEHN-chee EH oh-VEE-doo.
back: The report gave a voice to those who are rarely heard.
context: 'Dar voz a' = to give a voice to. 'Ser ouvido' = to be heard.

front: O jornalismo declaratório apenas reproduz o que as autoridades dizem.
pronunciation: oo zhohr-nah-LEEZ-moo deh-klah-rah-TOH-ryoo ah-PEH-nahs rreh-proh-DOOZ oo keh ahz ow-toh-ree-DAH-jeez JEE-zeng.
back: Statement-based journalism just repeats what officials say.
context: 'Jornalismo declaratório' = stenographic journalism, criticized for not checking claims.

front: O ombudsman criticou a cobertura parcial do próprio jornal.
pronunciation: oo ohm-boodz-MAHN kree-chee-KOH ah koh-behr-TOO-rah pahr-see-OW doo PROH-pree-oo zhohr-NOW.
back: The ombudsman criticized the newspaper's own biased coverage.
context: Folha de S.Paulo was the first Brazilian newspaper to have an ombudsman (1989). 'Cobertura' = coverage.

front: A ironia está no fato de o político defender o que antes condenava.
pronunciation: ah ee-roh-NEE-ah ehs-TAH noo FAH-too jee oo poh-LEE-chee-koo deh-fehn-DEHR oo keh AHN-cheez kohn-deh-NAH-vah.
back: The irony lies in the fact that the politician defends what he used to condemn.
context: Formal grammar: 'o fato de o político' (no contraction 'do' before the subject of an infinitive).

front: Esse texto é uma paródia do discurso motivacional corporativo.
pronunciation: EH-see TEHS-too EH OO-mah pah-ROH-jee-ah doo jees-KOOR-soo moh-chee-vah-syoh-NOW kohr-poh-rah-CHEE-voo.
back: This text is a parody of corporate motivational speeches.
context: 'Paródia' = parody; 'pastiche' = pastiche. Parody imitates in order to mock.

front: Ele disse com a cara mais lavada do mundo que não sabia de nada.
pronunciation: EH-lee JEE-see kohng ah KAH-rah MAHYS lah-VAH-dah doo MOON-doo keh NOWNG sah-BEE-ah jee NAH-dah.
back: He said with a perfectly straight face that he knew nothing.
context: 'Com a cara mais lavada do mundo' (with the most washed face) = brazenly, without shame.

front: Os leitores mais atentos perceberam a crítica escondida no título.
pronunciation: ooz lay-TOH-reez MAHYZ ah-TEHN-toos pehr-seh-BEH-rowng ah KREE-chee-kah ehs-kohn-JEE-dah noo CHEE-too-loo.
back: The more attentive readers noticed the criticism hidden in the title.
context: 'Atento' = attentive. 'Escondido' = hidden.

front: Em tempos de polarização, até a previsão do tempo vira polêmica.
pronunciation: eng TEHM-pooz jee poh-lah-ree-zah-SOWNG, ah-TEH ah preh-vee-ZOWNG doo TEHM-poo VEE-rah poh-LEH-mee-kah.
back: In times of polarization, even the weather forecast becomes controversial.
context: Ironic exaggeration. 'Virar polêmica' = to become controversial. 'Até' = even.

front: O correspondente cobriu a guerra por três anos.
pronunciation: oo koh-rrehs-pohn-DEHN-chee koh-BREE-oo ah GEH-rrah pohr TREHZ AH-noos.
back: The correspondent covered the war for three years.
context: 'Cobrir' = to cover (news). Past participle: 'coberto'.

front: O jornal impresso perdeu espaço para os portais e as redes sociais.
pronunciation: oo zhohr-NOW eem-PREH-soo pehr-DEH-oo ehs-PAH-soo PAH-rah oos pohr-TAHYZ ee ahz RREH-jees soh-SYAHYS.
back: Print newspapers lost ground to news websites and social media.
context: 'Perder espaço para' = to lose ground to. 'Portal (de notícias)' = news website.

front: Sem financiamento, o jornalismo local está desaparecendo e criando desertos de notícias.
pronunciation: seng fee-nahn-syah-MEHN-too, oo zhohr-nah-LEEZ-moo loh-KOW ehs-TAH jee-zah-pah-reh-SEHN-doo ee kree-AHN-doo deh-ZEHR-tooz jee noh-CHEE-syahs.
back: Without funding, local journalism is disappearing and creating news deserts.
context: 'Deserto de notícias' = news desert: a town with no local news outlet. A growing problem in Brazil.

front: Quem conta um conto aumenta um ponto.
pronunciation: KENG KOHN-tah oong KOHN-too ow-MEHN-tah oong POHN-too.
back: Every time a story is retold, it gets embellished.
context: Proverb: whoever tells a tale adds a stitch. A reminder of why journalists check sources directly.

front: A notícia é verdadeira, mas o enquadramento é enganoso.
pronunciation: ah noh-CHEE-syah EH vehr-dah-DAY-rah, mahz oo ehn-kwah-drah-MEHN-too EH ehn-gah-NOH-zoo.
back: The news is true, but the framing is misleading.
context: 'Enquadramento' = framing. 'Enganoso' = misleading. Advanced media literacy goes beyond true/false.

front: Se não fosse trágico, seria cômico.
pronunciation: see NOWNG FOH-see TRAH-zhee-koo, seh-REE-ah KOH-mee-koo.
back: If it weren't tragic, it would be funny.
context: A very common Brazilian comment on absurd political news, combining irony and resignation.
